title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities crosses spatial and taxonomic boundaries without detectable homogenization
frozen_core_claims: Recent-rain conditions are associated with two-dimensional expansion of the behaviourally realized acoustic community across active spatial footprint and taxonomic richness.
Local alpha and route gamma increase with rainfall contrast while measured among-active-site beta-diversity metrics show no detectable shift.
Active species x active-site matrix fill is practically equivalent within the prespecified margin.
About 92 percent of rainfall-associated species x stop incidence growth crosses at least one spatial and/or taxonomic matrix boundary; about 8 percent is within-core rearrangement.
The multiscale expansion signal persists under recorded detection-condition adjustments.
Across all 21 leave-one-state-out refits, active-footprint, local-alpha and route-gamma rainfall coefficients and their 95 percent confidence intervals remain positive.
frozen_geographic_interpretation: The pooled expansion signal is robust to omission of any single sampled state, but state-specific slopes are heterogeneous; this is not evidence for a uniformly positive effect in every state or continental universality.
frozen_mechanistic_interpretation: Heterogeneous species/site activation thresholds are a literature-supported plausible hypothesis for expansion without homogenization, not a causal mechanism identified by the present analysis.
frozen_negative_boundaries: No rainfall causality, occupancy, abundance, colonization, extinction or demographic-connectivity claim.
No claim that all states share the same effect direction or magnitude.
No species-level rainfall-response trait mechanism is authorized.
No week-long pulse or physiological half-life claim.
